rule_title: Warning and error messages displayed to clients must be modified to minimize the identity of the Apache web server, patches, loaded modules, and directory paths.
check_text:
Determine the location of the "HTTPD_ROOT" directory and the "httpd.conf" file:

# apachectl -V | egrep -i 'httpd_root|server_config_file'
-D HTTPD_ROOT="/etc/httpd"
-D SERVER_CONFIG_FILE="conf/httpd.conf"

Note: The apachectl front end is the preferred method for locating the Apache httpd file. For some Linux distributions, "apache2ctl -V" or "httpd -V" can also be used. 

# cat /<path_to_file>/httpd.conf | grep -i "ErrorDocument"

If the "ErrorDocument" directive is not being used for custom error pages for "4xx" or "5xx" HTTP status codes, this is a finding.

Note: Using a "sites-available" method for error messages is also acceptable; this would involve the use of /etc/apache2/sites-available and /etc/apache2/sites-enabled. As long as warning and error messages have been sanitized, this is not a finding.
